blocks.overview: This case concerns Applicant Zachary Ian Metz seeking judicial review of a Refugee Protection Division (RPD) decision granting refugee status to his children and their mother. The Respondent, Canada (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship), argues the Applicant lacks standing as he was not a party to the RPD proceedings. The Federal Court struck out the application for lack of standing, finding the Applicant was not directly affected by the RPD decision.

blocks.issue: Does the Applicant have standing to seek judicial review of the RPD decision granting refugee status to his children and their mother?
blocks.court_conclusion: Applicant is not directly affected and has no standing; application is struck out as clearly improper with no chance of success.

positions.text: Seeks authorization to launch judicial review and stay; disputes RPD finding he is agent of persecution; argues right to participate and cross-examine witnesses; claims serious collateral consequences on non-party.

Argues Applicant failed to establish standing; no direct interest; not a party; no legal obligations imposed; judicial review should not be entertained; relies on case law supporting motion to strike for lack of standing.
RPD found persons seeking protection were refugees under IRPA.

Applicant must establish standing; only directly affected persons may seek judicial review; standing can be decided preliminarily; Applicant not directly affected; no legal rights or obligations affected; application struck out.

propositions.text: Applicant Zachary Ian Metz is a Texas resident and litigant-in-person making a written motion under Federal Courts Rules Rule 369.
Applicant notes use of artificial intelligence in drafting documents but does not specify which parts.

Applicant's two children and their mother were granted refugee status in Canada.
Applicant learned of RPD decision on June 10 but filed judicial review application only on August 8.

propositions.text: Applicant concedes he was not a party to the proceedings before RPD.
Respondent argues Applicant failed to establish standing.

propositions.text: Applicant seeks authorization to launch judicial review and also seeks a stay of the RPD decision.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant seeks both authorization for judicial review and a stay of the RPD decision.

propositions.text: Applicant disputes RPD's finding he is the agent of persecution from whom children and mother seek protection.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant disputes the RPD's finding that he is the agent of persecution.

propositions.text: There are proceedings before Ontario courts involving the Hague Convention on International Child Abduction.
Very little is known about these Ontario proceedings which are outside federal jurisdiction.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes Ontario proceedings involving the Hague Convention exist but little is known and they are outside federal jurisdiction.

propositions.text: RPD found persons seeking Canada's protection were refugees under IRPA.
Some findings are raised in one fashion or another.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found persons seeking protection were refugees; some findings are raised in some manner.

propositions.text: Respondent opposes proceedings on basis Applicant has no standing to challenge RPD decision granting refugee status.
If no standing to launch judicial review, then no standing to be granted a stay.
Applicant is not a party to proceedings before this Court.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues applicant lacks standing to challenge RPD decision or to get a stay, as he is not a party before this Court.

propositions.text: Applicant seeks quashing of RPD decision because he was not allowed to participate in RPD proceedings.
Applicant invokes IRPA subsections 170(c) and (h) and common law procedural fairness duty.
Applicant argues he should have right to participate and cross-examine witnesses to deny refugee status.
Applicant does not explain how Ontario court proceedings prevent his participation where he has direct interest.
Respondent argues Applicant has no direct interest in RPD proceedings where refugee status is decided.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues he should have participated in RPD proceedings; respondent says he has no direct interest there.

propositions.text: Respondent moves to strike Applicant's challenge to RPD decision for lack of standing.
Applicant was not a party, no obligations imposed, relief does not prejudice him directly.
Applicant not directly affected; judicial review should not be entertained.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent moves to strike for lack of standing, arguing applicant not party, no obligations, no direct prejudice.

propositions.text: David Bull Laboratories test requires judicial review motion to strike be clearly improper with no possibility of success.
Court has jurisdiction to grant motion to strike but argument usually made before merits hearing.
David Bull Laboratories test stricter than traditional test for motions to strike for no reasonable claim.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains the strict David Bull Laboratories test for motions to strike judicial review applications.

propositions.text: Respondent argues standing requirement is completely lacking in this case.
Respondent relies on Canadian Generic Pharmaceutical Association case supporting motion to strike for lack of standing.
Canadian Generic Pharmaceutical Association found no standing justifies motion to strike judicial review.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues no standing here, relying on Canadian Generic Pharmaceutical Association supporting motion to strike.

propositions.text: Courts agree non-directly affected persons lack standing to challenge judicial review decisions.

paragraphs.summary: Courts agree that persons not directly affected lack standing to challenge judicial review decisions.

propositions.text: Respondent contends Federal Courts Act subsection 18.1(1) controls who can seek judicial review: only directly affected persons.
Matter must adversely affect legal rights, impose obligations, or prejudicially affect directly to have standing.
Forest Ethics Advocacy Association reaffirmed the direct effect test for standing.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues only persons directly affected under Federal Courts Act can seek judicial review, citing case law.

propositions.text: Respondent pleads any impact on Applicant is indirect and unknown.
Interest in Ontario court proceedings does not satisfy direct effect test for standing.
Soprema Inc. confirms parties to refugee proceedings are refugee claimant and Minister; rights of refugee are at issue.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues any impact on applicant is indirect; Ontario interest insufficient; refugee proceedings involve claimant and Minister rights.

propositions.text: Applicant not party to proceedings; no legal obligations imposed on him by RPD decision.
Ontario court proceedings not determined by RPD decision; Applicant can offer evidence there.
Kirby v Woods confirms Ontario courts determine family law matters on evidence before them.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues applicant not party, no obligations; Ontario courts decide family law matters independently, per Kirby v Woods.

propositions.text: Applicant cannot claim public interest standing as issue is family law matter for Ontario courts.
Ontario court is most reasonable and effective forum, not Federal Court judicial review of immigration matter.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues applicant lacks public interest standing; family law matter belongs in Ontario courts, not Federal Court review.

propositions.text: No right directly affected; Applicant lacks standing to seek judicial review of decision he did not participate in.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent concludes applicant lacks standing to seek judicial review of decision he did not participate in.

propositions.text: Family court cannot supply administrative law remedies, cannot review or set aside RPD decision, cannot compel Rule 317 production, cannot overcome IRPA s. 115
Not seeking public interest standing
Ontario Court cannot grant judicial review remedy; issue is whether Applicant has proper standing to challenge refugee status decision

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues family court cannot provide administrative remedies and is not seeking public interest standing; court finds issue is Applicant's standing to challenge refugee status decision.

propositions.text: Applicant must establish standing to judicially review RPD decision granting refugee status to his children and their mother
Federal Courts Act s.18 gives exclusive jurisdiction to Federal Court for judicial review of federal boards including Refugee Board
Section 18.1 specifies who may apply for judicial review: Attorney General or anyone directly affected

paragraphs.summary: Court states Applicant must prove standing to review RPD decision; Federal Courts Act grants exclusive jurisdiction and limits applicants to those directly affected.

propositions.text: Person must be directly affected by the matter to have standing for judicial review, not just feel affected

paragraphs.summary: Court states standing requires being directly affected by the matter, not merely feeling affected.

propositions.text: Case before RPD involves refugee status application, not family law
Relief sought is public law relief under federal statute granting refugee status

paragraphs.summary: Court notes case is refugee status application, not family law, and relief sought is public law under federal statute.

propositions.text: Applicant must establish standing to seek relief concerning someone else's refugee status
Notion of 'directly affected' has particular meaning recognized by Federal Courts
Forest Ethics Advocacy Association para 20 encapsulates meaning of 'directly affected' for standing

paragraphs.summary: Court states Applicant must prove standing to challenge another's refugee status; 'directly affected' meaning is established by Federal Courts and Forest Ethics case.

propositions.text: Court of Appeal says relief sought must affect legal rights, impose obligations, or prejudicially affect party directly
Applicant could not be added as respondent; immigration cases do not allow that
Relief granting refugee status will not affect Applicant's legal rights, obligations, or cause direct prejudice

paragraphs.summary: Court cites Court of Appeal on direct effect for standing; finds Applicant could not be respondent and refugee status relief does not directly affect him.

propositions.text: Applicant has no legal rights affected, no obligations imposed, no direct prejudice from refugee status decision
Applicant's concern is impact on unrelated family law litigation, not direct effect of refugee decision
Decision imposes serious collateral consequences on non-party
Applicant's concern about parental interest and reputation in different proceedings is not direct effect on refugee status
Applicant is not directly affected and has no standing to challenge refugee status decision

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Applicant not directly affected by refugee decision; his concerns relate to collateral effects in other proceedings; thus no standing.

propositions.text: Without standing, application is clearly improper and has no chance of success
Litigant must have standing to challenge administrative decision; Parliament requires direct effect
Standing can be decided preliminarily before merits, per Canadian Generic Pharmaceutical Association
Standing issue can be decided before judicial review proceeds

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes lack of standing makes application improper; standing is fundamental and can be decided preliminarily before merits.

propositions.text: Applicant submitted no argument or evidence showing standing to challenge refugee status decision

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Applicant submitted no evidence or argument to show standing to challenge refugee status decision.

propositions.text: Application for Leave and Judicial Review is struck out
Motion for stay of legal effect and enforcement of Refugee Protection decision is without object under s.18.2 Federal Courts Act

paragraphs.summary: Court strikes out application and finds motion for stay is without object under Federal Courts Act.

propositions.text: Respondent did not seek costs
No costs are granted
Applicant lacks standing to challenge June 4, 2025 Refugee Protection decision; application is struck out

paragraphs.summary: Respondent did not seek costs; court grants none; Applicant lacks standing and application is struck out.

propositions.text: Exception to general rule: issue of standing may be decided preliminarily if court has sufficient information (Apotex, Canwest, Finlay)
Record is sufficient to make final determination on standing
Court of Appeal agreed record suffices to decide standing
